newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - firmer bar steady fuel.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - firmer bar steady fuel.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were higher except fuel on tuesday.

Traders were mixed about high sulphur fuel with some saying that cracked material was tight and thus more expensive in the mid 80s while others saw the market as balanced with little supply but small demand also.
A seller of a cracked cargo was said to have lowered his price $1 to $89 cif with a buyer still holding his ground at $88.
Two cargoes of high sulphur straight-run fetched high cif Med quote plus $4 on Tuesday and Monday. A trader was said to be offering a cargo at high cif +$5.
Traders said that an indepedent trader won an Egyptian tender to lift 35,000-40,000 tonnes of high sulphur straight-run, on August 28-30.
One percent was quiet but traders said the market was tracking the north where swaps have firmed, so it should be notionally higher.
Gasoline values were seen notionally around $3 higher in the Med cargo market, in line with gains seen being made in the north.
Naphtha was seen quiet, but higher bid levels in the north for open spec and pipeline spec naphtha were seen helping to pull up values in the Med by $1-$2.
Gas oil was up to $4.00 in response to IPE gains and firmer NWE levels. Dealers said futures rose in response to late Monday gains on the Brent contract.
Supplies of Russian material were understood to be less well offered as refinery maintenance cuts into available supplies.
